Illustrative example: a house on a 4 m thick soft clay layer, allowable settlement 25 mm.
The piles transfer the load to the bearing stratum.
Most of the settlement took place before construction, under the preload.
The stone columns stiffen the layer and, acting as drains, speed up consolidation.
The top 1 m is replaced with good material; the deeper clay still settles.
The contact pressure is lower, but the effect reaches deeper: on its own it is not enough.
The whole 4 m thick soft clay layer is compressed.

If the calculated settlement or differential settlement is not acceptable with the chosen type of foundation, the design must be changed. Eight tools are available – from reducing the contact pressure through ground improvement to deep foundations.
